findings_v1.content: For a static HTML page (file:// URL, no server), the script MUST follow every one of these steps in order: (1) tell the user you read the HTML file first to identify real selectors (use the actual ids, names and labels from the file, never invented ones); if the file is not available, say so and mark which selectors are assumed; (2) launch chromium with `headless=True`; (3) `page.goto(Path('index.html').resolve().as_uri())`; (4) call `page.wait_for_load_state('networkidle')` right after goto, even for file:// pages; (5) call `browser.close()` at the end, in a `try/finally` when assertions are present. Never skip a step because the page looks simple.
findings_v1.rationale: The decision tree says to read static HTML to identify selectors, and the Best Practices require a headless launch, the networkidle wait and closing the browser. The previous answer used a file:// script but apparently skipped some of these steps.

findings_v1.content: When a test submits a form or triggers a UI change, do not check the result immediately. Wait explicitly first with `page.wait_for_selector(<success-selector>, state='visible')` or `expect(locator).to_be_visible()`, then assert the exact expected text with `expect(locator).to_contain_text(...)` or an `assert` on `locator.inner_text()`. Fill fields with `page.fill()` or `page.get_by_label()`, and click with `page.get_by_role('button', name=...)` or `page.click('text=...')`. Use the descriptive selectors the skill recommends: `text=`, `role=`, ids or CSS.
findings_v1.rationale: Concrete wait-then-assert rules make the form-submission check reliable and consistent with the skill's Best Practices.

findings_v1.content: Add basic diagnostics to every test script: register `page.on('console', lambda m: print('console:', m.text))`, and on failure (in an `except` block) call `page.screenshot(path='failure.png', full_page=True)` before re-raising. Also include one sentence saying that if the static-file approach fails or the page turns out to load content dynamically, you switch to the reconnaissance-then-action pattern (screenshot, then inspect the rendered DOM).
findings_v1.rationale: The skill's reference files show console logging, and its decision tree says a failed static approach falls back to the dynamic pattern. Making both explicit covers the debugging and fallback behavior the skill promises.
